data_fields.name: base_stat_formulas
data_fields.donor_constant: per-level formula over level and Str, Dex, Sta, Int, Spi, Fai (database rows, not read)

data_fields.name: equipment_flat_stat
data_fields.donor_constant: each equipped item adds its own flat value before the stack

data_fields.name: armour_piece_value
data_fields.donor_constant: sum of BaseArmor for armour and accessories, Armor for weapons (item data, not read)

data_fields.name: percent_bonus_unit
data_fields.donor_constant: value / 100 per percent bonus, applied to the running value (compounding)

data_fields.name: dynamic_bonus_ratio
data_fields.donor_constant: elapsed / duration clamped to 0..1; permanent buff counts as fully elapsed

data_fields.name: persistent_hp_regen_default
data_fields.donor_constant: 30 per call in battle (Unit default; Character overrides with a formula)

data_fields.name: regen_call_cadence
data_fields.donor_constant: about once per second for units in active player regions (comment; delta passed but unused in the add)

data_fields.name: death_xp_in_level_cap
data_fields.donor_constant: loss capped to XP earned in the current level

data_fields.name: regen_step_cap_proposed
data_fields.donor_constant: none in donor (proposed cap 1 s on the regen step)

best_idea: Compute every stat as one base formula plus flat equipment, then run one bonus stack in a fixed order (static flat, dynamic flat, static percent, dynamic percent) so buffs and gear combine the same way for every stat.
decision_why: Take the single stack and its fixed order for guard, parry, dodge, regen and damage stats, keep the percent rule explicit (percent compounds) in the catalogue, move base formulas to data, and fix the donor's per-call integer regen (no delta, truncated rate) in the sketch; the licence is unclear, so it is clean-room shape only.
acceptance: A server test asserts a 100 base with +10 flat gear and a +20 percent buff gives 132, that two +10 percent buffs on 100 give 121, and that health regen at 0.5 per second over four one-second steps gives exactly 2 points.
